# SPD-030 — Bash hook: CD, /usr/bin/cd, pushd and upper-case wrappers are read differently from the shell

## Brief
PreToolUse(Bash) follows the working directory and strips wrappers by command name. On macOS PATH lookup is case-insensitive (ENV, NOHUP, CD resolve to /usr/bin/ENV, /usr/bin/NOHUP, /usr/bin/CD) while shell builtins are not: the hook strips no wrapper named ENV or NOHUP, so a git write behind one is silent (Law 7), and it takes CD /tmp or /usr/bin/cd /tmp as a change of directory that never happens (the external cd runs in its own process), so a relative redirection lands in the repository unchecked (Laws 1 and 5). pushd and popd are not followed at all, and cd -P or cd -L takes the option for the directory. Not a spelling of the home, so outside SPD-029.

Evidence: Scratch SPUD_HOME, member with deliverable **, hook code before SPD-029 (SPD-029 does not change these): 'CD /tmp && echo x > ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md' silent; '/usr/bin/cd /tmp && echo x > ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md' silent; 'pushd <home>/ledger && echo x > tickets/SPD-001.md' silent; 'ENV git commit -m x' silent; 'NOHUP git push' silent. shutil.which: ENV -> /usr/bin/ENV, NOHUP -> /usr/bin/NOHUP, CD -> /usr/bin/CD. Fix sketch: casefold the name in the WRAPPERS test and strip_wrapper; treat only the exact word cd as the builtin; an option to cd, pushd or popd leaves a directory the hook cannot follow (cwd None, so a member's relative redirection is refused).

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus (the persona's tier), no children: the Bash hook's wrapper stripping and working-directory following in one function family, with red-first tests. No Fable today (Eric's budget). Code ticket: worktree spd-030-bash-hook-cd-wrappers.
